AUTHOR: Shah
TITLE: MI-AFR: multiple instance active learning-based approach for fish species recognition in underwater environments
VENUE: Proc. SPIE 12543, Ocean Sensing and Monitoring XV
REGION: Gulf of Mexico, USA (NOAA SEFSC reef fish video survey, SEAMAPD21 'Pascagoula data')
SPECIES: 51 most frequent reef fish species selected from the 130 SEAMAPD21 classes (not listed)
V_EV: Sec. 2: 'The major challenge in the SEAMAPD21 dataset is that it is underwater data with low light conditions and various levels of turbidity.' — no stratified results
D_EV: Sec. 3.5: 'The ratio of 70/15/15 is used for train, validation, and test set respectively.' (unit/randomness not stated)
R_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'Then, detection results in terms of mAP was evaluated on test set.' (SEAMAPD21 only)
C_EV: no statement found (instance uncertainty used only for active-learning sample selection; only 'We selected IOU of 0.45 to estimate mAP')
E_EV: Sec. 4.2: 'performance in terms of mAP estimated by averaging the average precision of 51 different fish species' — mAP only
ARCH: SSD300 / SSD512 detection head with VGG-16 or ResNet-50 backbone; MI-AOD-style active learning (two adversarial instance classifiers + MIL re-weighting)
METR: mAP (IoU 0.45) over 51 classes vs % labelled samples; best 65.80% (VGG-16, SSD512, 17.5% labelled); FPS 15-36
NOTE: Platform and habitat not described in the paper (merged.json: NOAA SEAMAP video survey cameras, marine reef fish; SEAMAPD21 is a predefined-by-image public split but the paper applies its own 70/15/15 ratio with unit unstated). NIMG is the full SEAMAPD21 size; the 51-class subset size is not given. The method estimates instance-level uncertainty (discrepancy between two adversarial classifiers) but only to select images for annotation, not to report or calibrate detection uncertainty, so C3 coded 없음 (verifier may consider 기타, which would make C_ALL = Y). Pre-training source of backbones not stated. Short proceedings paper; no ecological output.
